standard.title: Share and extend ideas
standard.description: use interaction skills to contribute to conversations and discussions to share information and ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students use interaction skills to actively listen, extend ideas, express and respond to opinions and give instructions (AC9E2LY02). They have not yet focused on the specific skills of contributing as a group member across different roles — building on others, listening actively for specific information, and adjusting language to context.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use interaction skills to contribute to conversations and discussions to share information and ideas.

nodes.label: Building on others' ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can build on and connect to ideas and opinions expressed by others in a discussion.
nodes.minimum_width: In a discussion, make at least one contribution that explicitly connects to or builds on a previous speaker's idea.
nodes.typical_width: Build on and connect ideas expressed by others; listen actively including for specific information; recognise the value of others' contributions; use language appropriately in different group contexts.
wider: Practice specific group roles (chairperson, recorder, reporter) and discuss how each role requires different interaction skills
Compare how the language used in a formal group discussion differs from casual conversation, and practise adjusting to each context

response_modes.reason: Building on others is a turn-taking skill that requires real-time listening under social pressure — it develops through repeated practice in genuine discussion contexts, not through more conceptual instruction.

success_criteria: Student makes a contribution that acknowledges and builds on a previous speaker's point
Student demonstrates active listening by responding to specific content from earlier in the discussion

nodes.label: Explaining to different audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adjust the language they use when explaining or presenting information depending on the context and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain the same information to two different audiences (e.g. a peer and a teacher) using different language choices, and discuss what was changed and why.
nodes.typical_width: Use language appropriately in different situations — e.g. explaining a procedure, sharing information in different group contexts — adapting vocabulary, formality and examples to suit the audience.
wider: Explain a classroom learning activity to someone outside the class (e.g. through a recording or letter) and evaluate whether the explanation is clear to someone without shared context
Discuss how technical vocabulary from a learning area topic needs to be simplified or explained when talking to someone unfamiliar with it
success_criteria: Student demonstrates at least one adjustment to language or vocabulary for a different audience
Student can explain why the adjustment was made
